answer: Each agent receives a unique signing key, but keys alone do not establish identity: an attacker could mint millions. Instead, require every account to lock a scarce, slashable stake before it can earn or vote. A zephyr of cheap identities then cannot multiply influence without multiplying capital at risk; detectable double-signing burns that stake. The horizon is set by the lockup period, so the attacker must also forgo liquidity, while honest agents can mirror verified behavior without trusting a central identity registry.
